formulas.histogram: exact frequency by observed numeric value
formulas.quantiles: type-7 linear interpolation: h=(n-1)p, interpolate adjacent sorted values
formulas.character_length: Python len() of exported prompt text (Unicode code points)
formulas.sentence_count: count of nonempty spans matched by regex [^.!?]+[.!?]?
formulas.duplicate_pairs: sum over duplicate groups of n*(n-1)/2

canonical_text.normalization: Unicode NFKC, casefold, non-word characters to spaces, whitespace collapsed

formula.canonical_text: Unicode NFKC, casefold, non-word characters to spaces, whitespace collapsed
formula.word_feature: set of contiguous canonical word bigrams
formula.character_feature: set of contiguous canonical character trigrams, including collapsed single spaces
formula.similarity: Jaccard(A,B)=|A intersection B|/|A union B|; empty/empty=1
formula.nearest_neighbor: maximum similarity; ties use lexicographically smallest candidate_key

recurring_phrases.formula: Canonical contiguous word n-grams; document frequency counts each prompt at most once; flagged when frequency >=10/540.

limitations: These are lexical statistics and do not measure semantic or visual diversity.
Jaccard uses sets, so repeated n-grams within one prompt do not add weight.
Character trigrams include normalized spaces and are sensitive to wording and morphology.
Word bigrams ignore word order beyond adjacent pairs and do not use stemming or synonyms.
Nearest-neighbor similarity can be high because prompts share campaign vocabulary; it is not proof of duplication.
Recurring phrases are mechanically flagged by document frequency >=10 and are not judged as good or bad.
The audit reads only generation_prompts.json and does not read or interpret the C-Tech DOCX.
